The answer is still **D**. GA resolutions are generally not binding, so A is wrong. They are not treaties, so B is wrong, and they do not always reflect customary law, so C is wrong. The team note limits the answer to B or C, but neither is legally correct. Resolutions can serve as a material source or as evidence of custom, because they may enunciate customary rules and show the opinio juris of the States that adopt them.
